messages:
cheng: quick RFC follow-up — we talked about moving region-aware enforcement into a lightweight sidecar on routers vs keeping a central chooser. putting the enforcer in the sidecar would let us apply tenant-local cost windows and immediate rejects before the control plane sees the request, but i worry about divergence and propagation delays. thoughts?

maya: high level tradeoffs: sidecar -> local fast decisions, cheaper RTT, works offline. central chooser -> single source of truth, easier audits, one place for rollouts. :thinking_face:

sam: from runtime POV sidecar wins for p99 latency. central chooser adds a hop and more coupling to control plane. sidecar complexity: policy hotreload, consistent blacklists, and ensuring no silent bypass.

laura: ops perspective: sidecars increase blast radius for bad policy pushes. we saw that when a miscompiled iptables rule went wide. central chooser lets us gate via rollout canaries and centralized kill-switch.

cheng: agree. can we design a hybrid: sidecar for fast evaluation with strict whitelisting of rule types, and central adjudicator for complex multi-tenant constraints? e.g., local enforcer can check single-tenant cost windows, but multi-tenant fairness gets kicked to central async path.

sam: that sounds reasonable. implementation notes: local enforcer must be deterministic, have a small memory footprint, and subscribe to a compact delta-stream for updates. if central says "override", sidecar should accept explicit signed overrides.

maya: product ask: we need clear semantics so SLA owners know when a request was dropped by local policy vs central capacity. need telemetry fields in the trace/span.

laura: add to that: central should emit events when it overrides or rescinds an override. we need retention for 90d for audits.

cheng: quick config sketch for local-enforcer allowed rule set (very rough):
```yaml
enforcer_version: 1
allowed_checks:
  - tenant_cost_window
  - route_region_affinity
  - token_quota_basic
blocked_checks_by_default: false
override_endpoint: https://control.internal/chooser/override
update_stream: kafka://policy-deltas
```

sam: runtime concerns: keep the rule language small. no arbitrary JS. prefer matchers like:
```
when (tenant_id == T && region == eu-west-1 && recent_cost > envelope) -> reject
```
We can implement this with a tiny rule VM.

laura: monitoring checklist: per-sidecar counters: evals_total, rejects_local, rejects_central_fallback, last_delta_seq. Also a health endpoint that returns policy_hash and last_applied_seq.

maya: UX note: customers should be able to opt into local enforcement. default for new tenants = central-only, opt-in migrates you to hybrid. can we support "dry-run" mode locally (log but don't reject)?

cheng: yes — sidecar should support mode: allow, dry-run, enforce. default dry-run during rollout.

sam: fallback safety: if sidecar update stream lags > 30s, switch to central-only mode. avoid stale enforcement.

laura: ops fallback: add a kill-switch that can flip all sidecars to central-only for a region. expose to a runbook and SRE playbooks.

kevin-bot: deploy-bot: deployment note — sidecar image bump v0.9.3 will include policy-delta consumer and health endpoints. staging rollout scheduled 2026-05-14 22:00 UTC. :rocket:

maya: question for SRE: what does rollout look like? can we stagger by AZ or by tenant cohort?

laura: stagger by AZ first, then tenant-cohort. steps: 1) dry-run AZ1 (24h metrics), 2) enable enforce for low-risk cohorts, 3) expand. metrics to watch: local_rejects/requests, error_rate, end-to-end p99.

sam: perf micro-impl note: keep cache for tenant envelope lookups, LRU with 1000 entries per sidecar. add quick path for cached accept decisions to avoid rule eval CPU for steady traffic.

cheng: open question — where do we store the authoritative tenant envelopes? central control-plane DB (postgres) or a fast kv (redis)? prefer kv for low-latency fetch during on-boot sync.

laura: prefer redis with versioned keys and fallback to DB for rebuilds. ensure we have reconciliation job to detect drift.

maya: timeline: aim for design doc this week, prototype next sprint, canary in staging after two sprints.

cheng: thanks all. i'll draft a short RFC update with the hybrid pattern, required telemetry fields, and rollout checklist. tagging @laura @sam for review. :eyes:

sam: quick nit — include explicit semantics for tie-breaking when local and central disagree (central wins, unless sidecar has signed override token).

laura: also log the decision predicate in structured form so postmortem queries are easy.

cheng: noted. i'll include examples of structured telemetry and a sample trace span fields.
